Title: User registers and logs in successfully
Preconditions: Backend server running on http://localhost:8000; Streamlit UI running on http://localhost:8501; no existing user with the test username
Steps: 1. Open the Streamlit app in a browser | 2. Click the "Create account" tab | 3. Enter username, email, and password | 4. Click "Create account" | 5. Switch to "Login" tab | 6. Enter the same username and password | 7. Click "Log in"
Expected Result: Account is created successfully; login succeeds and the app shows the main dashboard with "Welcome, janedoe!" and a sidebar logout button

Title: Full login session persists across page interactions until logout
Preconditions: User janedoe already registered via TC-001; backend and UI both running
Steps: 1. Log in as janedoe via the Login tab | 2. Verify sidebar shows "Logged in as janedoe" | 3. Interact with the welcome page | 4. Click "Log out" in the sidebar | 5. Verify the login page reappears | 6. Attempt to call GET /api/auth/me with the previously issued token
Expected Result: Session token is stored for the duration of the login, the UI reflects logged-in state, logout clears session state and returns to the login page; the token used before logout remains valid until expiry since this app does not implement server-side revocation

Title: Login attempt with expired or malformed JWT token is rejected
Preconditions: Backend server running; ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES set to a short value or a manually crafted invalid token is available
Steps: 1. Obtain a valid access token via POST /api/auth/login | 2. Wait until the token expires (or tamper with the token string) | 3. Send GET /api/auth/me with the expired/tampered token in the Authorization header
Expected Result: API responds with HTTP 401 Unauthorized and detail "Could not validate credentials"

Title: Registering a new unique user returns the created user profile
Preconditions: Backend server running; no existing user with username "newuser123"
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/auth/register with a unique username, valid email, and password of at least 8 characters | 2. Inspect the JSON response
Expected Result: API responds with HTTP 201 Created and a JSON body containing id, username, and email fields, with no password or hashed_password field present

Title: Registering with a duplicate username is rejected
Preconditions: A user with username "bob" already exists in the database
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/auth/register with username "bob" and a different email/password | 2. Inspect the response status and body
Expected Result: API responds with HTTP 400 Bad Request and detail "Username already registered"; no duplicate row is created in the users table

Title: Login with incorrect password is rejected
Preconditions: A user with username "dave" already exists with a known password
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/auth/login with username "dave" and an incorrect password | 2. Inspect the response status and body
Expected Result: API responds with HTTP 401 Unauthorized with detail "Incorrect username or password"; no access token is returned

Title: Registration rejects password shorter than minimum length
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/auth/register with a password shorter than 8 characters | 2. Inspect the response status
Expected Result: API responds with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity due to Pydantic field validation on the password length

Title: Registration rejects an invalid email format
Steps: 1. Send POST /api/auth/register with a malformed email address | 2. Inspect the response status
Expected Result: API responds with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity due to EmailStr validation failure

Title: UI shows a clear error when the backend is unreachable
Preconditions: Streamlit UI running but the FastAPI backend process is stopped or BACKEND_URL points to an unreachable host
Steps: 1. Open the Streamlit app | 2. Enter valid-looking credentials in the Login form | 3. Click "Log in"
Expected Result: UI displays an error message "Could not reach the backend: ..." instead of crashing, and the user remains on the login page
